(Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- nori-change-documenter: Creates documentation about changes to a codebase. Call the nori-change-documenter whenever you change the codebase. Provide all of the relevance context for *why* the change was made. Be extremely detailed! Provide as much context as possible so the agent can accurately update documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the nori-codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-locator: Locates files, directories, and components relevant to a feature or task. Call `nori-codebase-locator` with human language prompt describing what you're looking for. Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring to use one of these tools more than once. (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-pattern-finder: nori-codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like nori-codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- nori-initial-documenter: Creates documentation about a codebase. This agent creates the initial documentation for the codebase; use this agent when you want to create documentation and no existing documentation is present. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the nori-web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run nori-web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- reviewer: High-judgment read-only review. Use to check a diff or design for correctness bugs, edge cases, and simpler alternatives before integrating - especially work produced by builder agents. Returns findings with file:line references and severity; does not fix anything.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

Use for searches, file inventories, "where is X defined/used", summarizing a file or directory, running read-only bd/git commands or tests and reporting output verbatim. No editing. Delegate here whenever the task is mechanical lookup rather than judgment. Prefer calling `scripts/codex-agent scout` directly from the orchestrator when you can (same isolation, no relay hop; include the recon rules from this file in the prompt); this agent type is the interface for workflow agentType calls and the fallback when codex is unavailable.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- quota-watch: Monitor Amp Free quota and handoff before exhaustion. Use when user says quota-watch, check quota, or monitor usage.
- initialize-noridocs: Initialize docs.md files throughout the codebase
- nori-create-skillset: Create a new custom skillset by cloning an existing skillset
- nori-switch-skillset: Switch between Nori configuration skillsets (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- session-close: Cold-start-readiness check before ending a work session - runs the 3 judgment prompts plus the mechanical backstop, then the standard close/push.
- setup-beads-sync: Set up a private GitHub Dolt repo for personal beads and configure sync for the current project
- switch-nori-profile: Switch between Nori configuration profiles (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- triage: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

{
  "title": "Design safe embedded ↔ proxied copy migration with rollback",
  "status": "open",
  "assignee": null,
  "desc": "Design and verify a copy-based migration from the default embedded managed-local database under .beads/embeddeddolt into managed-local proxied storage under .beads/dolt, plus the reverse journey. Current migrate-dolt-mode support only flips metadata between server/shared-server and proxied-server when they already share the same database directory; it does not move an embedded database or provide a live-data transition."
}

{
  "title": "Harden managed proxy identity and listener-safety contract",
  "status": "open",
  "assignee": null,
  "desc": "Make managed proxied startup and stale recovery prove that ports and PIDs belong to the expected workspace proxy and Dolt child before connecting to or killing them. Current endpoint discovery accepts a listener on the PID-file loopback port without a protocol identity handshake, stale cleanup can kill a reused PID, PickFreePort has a bind-close-launch race, and a caller-supplied Dolt YAML can override the generated loopback-only backend host without validation."
}

{
  "title": "Define the supported local Dolt executable install and version contract",
  "status": "open",
  "assignee": null,
  "desc": "Define how managed-local proxied mode obtains and validates the separate dolt executable required by exec.LookPath. Current behavior assumes an arbitrary dolt on PATH and provides no supported-version range, checksum/provenance rule, platform packaging guarantee, upgrade policy, or actionable doctor output. This gap is distinct from upstream #4512, which concerns the embedded Go module pseudo-version rather than the CLI executable."
}

if [ "$tier" = reviewer ]; then

My findings are concentrated on Windows semantics and on recovery paths that have no escape hatch.

## Findings

### 1. blocker — `cleanupOrphanBackend` holds the process handle while waiting for exit; on Windows this can never succeed
`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/endpoint.go:769-792`

```go
handle, dead, err := openRecordedProcess(pf)   // 769
...
defer func() { _ = handle.Close() }()          // 785  <-- still open below
if err := handle.Kill(); err != nil { ... }    // 787

So `procid.Verify` (`procid_windows.go:29-43`) keeps returning `matched=true` for the terminated backend, `waitForRecordedProcessExit` burns its full `backendExitTimeout` (5s) and returns "timeout waiting for process exit", which fails `spawnAndHandoff` and therefore fails `GetCreateDatabaseProxyServerEndpoint`. `shutdown.go:260-268` gets this right (`handle.Close()` *before* `waitForRecordedProcessExit`), which makes the endpoint.go ordering look like an oversight rather than a deliberate difference.

```go

if err := handle.Close(); err != nil { return ... }
if err := waitForRecordedProcessExit(pf, backendExitTimeout); err != nil { ... }

and drop the `defer`.

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/procid/procid_windows.go:29-43`

Fix: after `OpenProcess` succeeds, call `windows.GetExitCodeProcess` and treat anything other than `STILL_ACTIVE` (259) as not-matching. `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/shutdown.go:63-68` and `force_stop.go:46-94`

The only remaining recovery is manual file surgery; `PurgeControlFiles` is reachable only from `cmd/bd/migrate_dolt_mode.go:390`.

- Renaming/moving the project directory while the proxy is running (the running proxy keeps `proxy.lock` on the same inode, so the lock stays held under the new path).

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/force_stop.go:152-202`

The PR description and `doltStopCmd`'s help both present the basename check as the safety property; it is much weaker than that reads.

Fix: add a workspace-scoping check before signaling. On Linux, read `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and require it to contain `rootDir` (the proxy child is spawned as `db-proxy-child --root <rootDir>`, `endpoint.go:414-420`); on Windows, `QueryFullProcessImageName` plus the command line via WMI/`NtQueryInformationProcess`, or fall back to requiring the recorded data port to be bound by that PID. `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/control.go:86-97` wired to `server.go:232-239`

Three consecutive `Accept` errors within ~30ms (10ms + 20ms backoff) push an error onto `s.errs`, which the errgroup treats as fatal and shuts down the proxy *and its backend*. Losing the control listener degrades adoption (callers fall back to the poll/retry path, which is already correct) but should not take down data service.

### 6. minor — the client discloses the secret to a peer it has not yet authenticated
`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/storage/dbproxy/identity/control.go:57`

`Identify` writes `IDENT <secret> <nonce>` in cleartext to whatever is listening on `pf.ControlPort` before the server proves anything. In the current flow this is gated by a passing `procid.Verify` on the recorded PID, so a mis-bound port is hard to reach — but the disclosure is avoidable at zero cost: send `HMAC(secret, nonce_client)` instead of the raw secret and have the server verify that, keeping the existing reply MAC as the server's proof. That makes the exchange a real mutual challenge-response and removes the secret from the wire entirely.

### 7. minor — the control port is reachable by any local user; slot exhaustion is a cheap `bd` DoS
`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/control.go:41,51,100-108`

`maxConcurrentIdentRequests = 8` with a 2s deadline; any unprivileged local user can hold all 8 slots indefinitely (connections beyond that are closed immediately, `control.go:106-107`). Legitimate `Identify` calls then get `ErrIdentRefused` → `adoptionIdentityMismatch` → 15s `openDeadline` → every `bd` command fails while the proxy is healthy. This is a new vector introduced by the control listener.

Fix: prefer a unix socket with 0600 (named pipe on Windows) over TCP loopback, or check `SO_PEERCRED`/`LOCAL_PEERCRED` uid on accept. Cheaper partial mitigation: don't let a slow peer occupy a slot — read the request line with a sub-second deadline before consuming a slot.

### 8. minor — schema forward-compat is inconsistent (`>=` in the pidfile, `==` in the handshake)
`pidfile/pidfile.go:41-43` accepts `Schema >= SchemaV2`, but `endpoint.go:569` requires `reply.Schema != pidfile.SchemaV2` to fail. A future schema-3 proxy is therefore accepted by the pidfile validator but rejected by the handshake, giving `adoptionIdentityMismatch` while the v3 proxy holds `proxy.lock` — an old `bd` in a mixed-version workspace hard-fails after 15s with a misleading "identity does not match" error. Pick one policy; if the intent is "v2 or newer", relax the reply check to `reply.Schema < pidfile.SchemaV2`.

### 9. minor — `requireUnverifiableProxyRecord` fails open on a `RootID` error
`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/force_stop.go:143-149`

```go
rootID, err := identity.RootID(rootDir)
if err == nil && record.RootID == rootID { return errors.New(...use proxy.Shutdown) }
return nil
```
When `RootID` errors, the guard silently takes the *more destructive* branch and lets force-stop signal a record that may in fact be perfectly verifiable. Return the error instead of swallowing it.

### 10. minor — `killSpawnedChild` refuses to kill our own child and leaks it
`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/endpoint.go:893-895`

If `procid.Open` failed for any non-gone reason at `endpoint.go:499-505`, `child.handle` is nil and the timeout path returns "verified process handle for pid %d is unavailable" without killing anything — the child proxy is left running and unparented while `spawnAndHandoff` returns an error. For our *own* not-yet-reaped child, `child.cmd.Process.Kill()` is safe (the PID cannot be recycled before `Wait` returns) and is strictly better than leaking. Suggest falling back to `child.cmd.Process.Kill()` when `handle == nil`.

### 11. nit — birth token captured after `cmd.Start()` has a theoretical reuse window
`endpoint.go:499` and `server/doltserver.go:266-267` capture the token after the child exists; if the child exits instantly and the PID is recycled before `Capture`, the pidfile records a foreign process's token, which a later `cleanupOrphanBackend` would then verify and kill. The window requires PID-space wraparound between two adjacent syscalls, so this is theoretical, but it is the one place where the whole birth-token scheme can record a wrong-but-self-consistent identity. Worth a comment at minimum.

### 12. nit — direct error comparison instead of `errors.Is`
`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-proxy-identity/internal/procid/procid_windows.go:32`: `if err == windows.ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`. Every other site in this PR (including `IsProcessGone` two functions below) uses `errors.Is`. It happens to work today because `OpenProcess` returns a bare `Errno`, but it will silently stop working if the call is ever wrapped.

## Test coverage gaps (riskiest paths)

- **No Windows tests at all.** Every lifecycle test is `_linux_test.go`/`_unix_test.go`; `procid_windows.go` and `process_executable_windows.go` have zero coverage. Findings (1), (2) and (12) are all Windows-only and all would have been caught by a `procid_windows_test.go` that terminates a child, keeps a handle open, and asserts `Verify` reports gone. Given the release-blocker framing, at least one Windows CI lane exercising `TestShutdownVerifiedRecordStopsProcess` and the orphan-backend reap is worth having; `.github/workflows/proxied-local-smoke.yml` is Linux-only.
- **No test for the root-mismatch recovery path.** `TestShutdownRefusesForeignRootProxyRecord` (`endpoint_security_test.go:681`) asserts the refusal; nothing asserts the operator can get *out* of that state (finding 3). A test that renames the workspace root under a live proxy and asserts a documented recovery would pin the contract.
- **No test for secret rotation racing an in-flight `Identify`.** `TestSecret_WriteReadAndRotate` covers the file, but the interesting case is a `readAndDial` that read secret S1 and dials a proxy that has since rotated to S2 — the code handles it by retrying, but that convergence is untested.
- **No test for `killSpawnedChild` with a nil handle** (finding 10) — the branch is unreachable in tests today.
- `TestControl_AcceptLoopStopsAfterPersistentErrors` pins the current fail-fast behavior; if finding 5 is addressed, that test needs to change with it.

## Verdict

**NEEDS-FIXES** — blocking: (1) `cleanupOrphanBackend` holding the procid handle across `waitForRecordedProcessExit`, which makes Windows crashed-proxy recovery fail unconditionally. Strongly recommended before land: (2) Windows `Verify` exit-code check, (3) the no-recovery root-ID mismatch, and (4) workspace-scoping the `--force` kill.</result>

`endpoint.go:499` and `server/doltserver.go:266-267` capture the token after the child exists; if the child exits instantly and the PID is recycled before `Capture`, the pidfile records a foreign process's token, which a later `cleanupOrphanBackend` would then verify and kill.     physRoot := fileCfg.DatabasePath(beadsDir)
    if fileCfg.GetDoltMode() == configfile.DoltModeEmbedded {
```

The real open path (`internal/storage/dolt/open.go:110-160`) resolves the mode through four layers that this code skips:

- `applyCentralConfigDefaults(fileCfg)` (open.go:124) can set `DoltMode` from `~/.config/beads/server.json` (`internal/configfile/central_config.go:66-68`). `OpenGated` never applies it.

`beads.go:299`

But the codebase explicitly supports that layout: `internal/beads/beads.go:507-514` has a "check if embeddeddolt or dolt directory exists without metadata.json" fallback. Such a workspace opens a real embedded DB with only the workspace gate held — and the workspace gate does not cover a `bd doctor --fix` integrity recovery, which renames `getDatabasePath(beadsDir)` out from under it (`cmd/bd/doctor/fix/database_integrity.go:46`).

`os.OpenFile(g.path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_RDWR, 0o600)`. The package doc explicitly names `~/.beads/shared-server/dolt` as a physical root (gate.go:167-170). `internal/workspacegate/gate.go:447-458`

`forDir` canonicalizes symlinks via `EvalSymlinks` but not case: on macOS/APFS-CI and Windows, `EvalSymlinks` returns the caller's spelling. Two consequences:

- Dedupe miss: two `Gate`s that name the same file with different case do not collapse, so `AcquireAll(..., Exclusive, ...)` opens it twice and the second flock conflicts with the first — a guaranteed self-block for the whole wait budget.
- Ordering divergence: two processes spelling a shared path differently sort their gate sets differently, inverting the acquisition order. Bounded waits keep this a livelock rather than a deadlock, but both processes can burn their full budget and fail.

Fix: derive a comparison key that lowercases on `runtime.GOOS` in `{windows, darwin}` and use it for both the `uniq` map and the `sort.Slice` comparator (keep `g.path` as the open path).

`internal/workspacegate/gate.go:227-228`

The `mode == Shared` branch returns the sidecar description unqualified, skipping the `pidAlive` check the Exclusive branch gets. The justifying comment (gate.go:201-203) assumes the sidecar always tracks the current exclusive holder, but `writeInfo` is best-effort and swallows every failure (gate.go:374-412) — ENOSPC, a read-only parent, or losing the `O_EXCL` race all leave the *previous*, dead holder's record in place while a live holder blocks you. Fix: apply the same `pidAlive` qualification in the Shared branch; it costs one syscall on an already-failing path.

### 7. MINOR — the embedded physical gate lives *inside* `.beads`, against the package's own stated rule
`internal/workspacegate/gate.go:11-20` vs. `beads.go:302`

The doc says gate files "deliberately live in a stable parent directory OUTSIDE every root a gated operation may replace". For embedded mode the guarded root is `.beads/embeddeddolt`, so the gate lands at `.beads/embeddeddolt.gate.lock` — inside `.beads`. `internal/workspacegate/gate.go:503`

`os.OpenFile(g.path, os.O_RDWR, 0o600)` fails with EACCES on a gate file owned by another user, even though both `flock(LOCK_SH)` and `LockFileEx` shared need only read access. Change to `os.O_RDONLY` to widen the diagnostic's reach (compounds with finding 4).

### 9. NIT — the `writeInfo` nolint rationale is inaccurate
`internal/workspacegate/gate.go:392-393`

The comment credits `O_EXCL` with refusing pre-planted files, but the `os.Remove(tmp)` on the preceding line already deletes any plant — `O_EXCL` is what closes the remove→open re-plant window, which is a different (and worth stating) property. The code is correct; the comment describes the wrong mechanism.

### 10. NIT — `pidAlive` leaks a Windows process handle
`internal/workspacegate/gate.go:240-258`

`os.FindProcess` on Windows opens a real handle that is only freed by `Wait`/`Release`. Add `defer p.Release()`. Bounded at ≤2 calls per acquisition today, so impact is negligible — but it is free to fix.

### 11. NIT — a failed `Close` strands the gate with no escape hatch
`beads.go:349-354`

Holding the flock after a failed `Close` is the right default and is well argued in the comment. But a long-lived embedder that hits repeated close failures accumulates fds and permanently blocks exclusive maintenance in that process, with no way to say "I've confirmed quiescence, release anyway". Consider exposing `func (g *gatedStorage) ForceReleaseGate() error` (or documenting the "restart the process" remedy on `OpenGated`).

- **No test that `OpenGated`'s physical gate path matches the store's actual data dir.** `beads_gated_test.go` only exercises the workspace gate; findings 1 and 2 would both have been caught by a table test over `{embedded, server, proxied-server, shared-server-env, central-config-mode, no-metadata.json}` asserting the gate path.
- **`busyDetail`/`pidAlive` staleness logic is entirely untested** (grep for `pidAlive|busyDetail|readInfo` in `gate_test.go` returns nothing; `pidAlive` is at 54.5%). This is the subtlest code in the file — a test that writes a sidecar with a known-dead PID and asserts the "stale record was ignored" wording is cheap.
- **No cross-process `AcquireAll` ordering test.** `TestAcquireAllSortsDedupesAndCleansUp` asserts sort order within one process only; nothing exercises two processes contending for an overlapping gate set (finding 5).
- **No test for gate-file creation failure on a read-only parent** — the path where a single unwritable directory fails every gated command (relevant to part-2 CLI wiring, and to finding 4).
- **`ExclusiveHolder`'s error return** (the "must not treat as not-held" contract) is untested; only the held/free branches are.

There are now three independent derivations of "the physical root for this workspace": `internal/beads/beads.go:471-514`, `internal/storage/dolt/open.go:227-228` + `doltserver.ResolveServerDir`, and `beads.go:299-303`. The third is the one that is wrong. Collapsing them into one exported helper would fix findings 1 and 2, delete code rather than add it, and give part 2 a single place to wire the CLI.

## What's sound

I specifically tried to break the things you asked about, and these held up:

- **Lock ordering / deadlock.** Sorted canonical-path total order in `AcquireAll` is correct, and every wait is bounded, so even a caller who violates the "one AcquireAll" invariant gets `ErrBusy` rather than a permanent wedge. Only finding 5 perturbs this, and only into bounded livelock.
- **Crash recovery.** flock/`LockFileEx` are both released by the kernel on process death, and the sidecar is advisory-only with the lock as sole authority. **A dead holder cannot wedge future invocations** — `TestCrashReleasesLock` and `TestSpawnedChildDoesNotInheritGate` cover this directly, and the close-on-exec reasoning about a `dolt` child outliving its parent is correct.
- **Gate-file placement vs. inode splitting.** The reasoning at gate.go:11-20 is right, and I verified the one real destructive op (`database_integrity.go:46`) renames the guarded root while leaving the sibling gate file intact.
- **Symlink handling.** Refusing a symlinked guarded directory rather than gating it ambiguously (gate.go:146-148) is the correct call, and the `EvalSymlinks`-the-parent-only rule genuinely does keep identity stable across the guarded dir being absent/created/replaced.
- **Sidecar write.** `O_EXCL` temp + rename correctly avoids both symlink-following and torn reads; `TestInfoSidecarDoesNotFollowSymlink` is a good test.
- **Release-before-unlock ordering** (gate.go:286-291) is subtle and correct.
- **TOCTOU.** No gap between acquisition and the guarded operation — the handle is held throughout.
- **Cooperative-only enforcement** is honestly documented (gate.go:31-36) rather than oversold.

## Verdict

**NEEDS-FIXES** — blocking on finding 1 (`OpenGated` gates the wrong physical root under central-config / env / config.yaml / shared-server / case-variant mode resolution) and finding 2 (no physical gate at all when metadata.json is absent but a database directory exists). Both are in `beads.go:299-303` and both are fixed by the single shared resolver suggested above.

The `internal/workspacegate` primitive — which is what the PR title scopes as part 1 — is land-ready on its own. If you want to unblock the series quickly, dropping `OpenGated` and `ErrGateBusy` from this PR and landing the primitive plus the gitignore wiring is a clean split; the public API can land with part 2's resolver.</result>

- No coverage for `remotesapi.port` / `cluster` / `listener.socket` (findings 1-2) — because unimplemented.

**6. MINOR (simpler alternative, fixes 5) — five scattered `validateManagedListenerHost` calls should be one.**
`ensureProxiedServerConfig` now calls the validator at lines 288, 331, 341, 363 plus `renderProxiedServerConfig:539`. Fix: thread `serverRootPath` into the helper, or move the call to after the sidecar is persisted.

**10. NIT — redundant branch.** `proxied_server.go:473-475` re-runs `validateProxiedServerConfig(explicitPath)`, which `init.go:338` already ran for the same value under the same condition.

**11. MINOR — the surviving `PickFreePort` writes an *ephemeral-range* port into `config.yaml` permanently, with no recovery.**
`proxied_server.go:373` picks from the kernel's ephemeral range (Linux 32768-60999) and persists it; `ensureProxiedServerConfig` only generates when the file is absent, and `grep` finds no `EADDRINUSE`/repick handling anywhere in `internal/storage/dbproxy/` or `cmd/bd/proxied_server.go`. So a collision after reboot bricks the workspace until a human edits YAML. The code comment defers this to "the PR-C RFC", which is a reasonable scope call, but this is a *user-visible* known failure mode being shipped.
Fix: at minimum a CHANGELOG "known limitation" entry; ideally, on backend start failure, repick + rewrite for marker-owned configs only.
(Platform note: no SO_REUSEADDR concern here — Go sets it on unix listeners only, and an accept-less listener leaves no TIME_WAIT on Windows, so the remaining race is pure "someone else grabbed it", identical on both platforms.)

**12. MINOR — flag help and docs not updated for a new hard constraint.**
`init.go` flag help for `--proxied-server-config-path` (mirrored at `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/review-psxg5-listener-policy/docs/cli-reference/init.md:67`) still reads "bd uses this file instead of auto-generating one" with no mention that non-loopback / hostname listeners are now rejected. Same for `BEADS_PROXIED_SERVER_CONFIG`. Everything is EXPERIMENTAL so the blast radius is small, but the remediation text is the only place a user learns the rule.

**13. NIT — the new e2e test re-creates the race it is testing around.**
`cmd/bd/proxied_local_listener_policy_linux_test.go:52` calls `proxy.PickFreePort()` and hands the port to a dolt backend started much later — the exact bind-close-launch window this PR removes elsewhere. Acceptable in a test, but it's a latent flake in CI.

- No coverage for `remotesapi.port` / `cluster` / `listener.socket` (findings 1-2) — because unimplemented.

- No coverage for `validateManagedProxiedServerConfigAtInit` with `--proxied-server-root-path` (finding 9).
- No end-to-end coverage that a fixed `--proxied-server-port` still yields a working proxy (only that the default is 0, at `proxied_local_helpers_test.go:75`).

**NEEDS-FIXES** — blocking: (1) `remotesapi.port`/`cluster` bypass and (2) `listener.socket` + the implicit `/tmp/mysql.sock`, which together mean the PR's stated invariant ("managed proxied mode must never expose a non-loopback listener") does not hold; and (3) the omitted-vs-`localhost` asymmetry, which must be resolved in one direction or the other before this is defensible policy. (5) should land with them since fix (6) resolves it for free. Everything else is minor/nit and can follow.</result>

# Fix spec for PR gastownhall/beads#5013 (branch feat/psxg5-proxy-identity)

Worktree: /var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/fix-5013
All findings verified by two independent reviewers (Claude opus + Codex gpt-5.6-sol). Fix ALL items below on this branch. #5024 is stacked on this branch, so lifecycle fixes belong here.

## Blocking

### B1. cleanupOrphanBackend holds the process handle across waitForRecordedProcessExit (Windows: recovery always fails)
`internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/endpoint.go:769-792`. An open handle on Windows keeps the PID allocated, so `procid.Verify` keeps matching the dead process and `waitForRecordedProcessExit` times out — every orphan-backend cleanup fails and the workspace cannot restart. `shutdown.go:260-268` already does this correctly.
Fix: drop the `defer handle.Close()`; close the handle explicitly BEFORE `waitForRecordedProcessExit`, mirroring shutdown.go:
```go
if err := handle.Kill(); err != nil { _ = handle.Close(); return ... }
if err := handle.Close(); err != nil { return ... }
if err := waitForRecordedProcessExit(pf, backendExitTimeout); err != nil { ... }
```

### B2. procid Windows Verify reports a terminated process as still matching
`internal/procid/procid_windows.go:29-43`. Any third party holding a handle (Task Manager, AV, debugger) keeps the PID resolvable, so Verify returns true for a dead process. Fix: after OpenProcess succeeds, call `windows.GetExitCodeProcess` and treat anything other than STILL_ACTIVE (259) as not-matching. Make the invariant "Verify==true implies running" hold on all platforms.

# Fix spec for PR gastownhall/beads#5046 (branch feat/workspace-gate)

Worktree: /var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/workspace-gate (branch checkout, clean)

Decision (orchestrator): take the reviewer's split option. This PR lands the `internal/workspacegate` primitive ONLY. The `OpenGated`/`ErrGateBusy` public API in `beads.go` moves to part 2, where a single shared physical-root resolver will fix its mode-resolution defects. Rationale: the reviewer found the primitive land-ready but `OpenGated` gates the wrong physical root under central-config/env/shared-server resolution (blocker) and skips the gate when metadata.json is absent (blocker); both are fixed by a resolver that part 2 needs anyway.

## Work items

### 1. Split out the public API
Remove `OpenGated`, `ErrGateBusy`, and the `gatedStorage` wrapper from `beads.go` (and their tests in `beads_gated_test.go`) from THIS branch. Keep the `internal/workspacegate` package, its tests, and any .gitignore wiring. Preserve the removed code in a note for part 2: copy the removed hunks into `/tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/e4d4db15-8aa8-49e2-abb1-e56fa80987d6/scratchpad/opengated-part2-carryover.md` with a short header explaining the two blockers to fix when it returns (wrong physical-root derivation vs internal/storage/dolt/open.go:110-160 four-layer resolution; nil-config skip vs internal/beads/beads.go:507-514 fallback).

### 2. Cheap primitive fixes (all in internal/workspacegate/gate.go)
a. Starvation: document on `Exclusive` and `Options.Wait` that rolling shared holders can starve an exclusive acquirer indefinitely (LOCK_NB polling, no intent signal); note the intent-marker idea as a future extension. Doc-only.
b. Case-insensitive filesystems: derive a comparison key (lowercase when runtime.GOOS is windows/darwin) and use it for BOTH the dedupe map and the sort comparator in `AcquireAll` (gate.go:447-458); keep g.path as the open path.
c. `busyDetail` Shared branch (gate.go:227-228): apply the same `pidAlive` qualification the Exclusive branch has, so a dead recorded holder is reported as stale, not fact.
d. `ExclusiveHolder` (gate.go:503): open O_RDONLY instead of O_RDWR (read-only probe; widens reach on foreign-owned gate files).
e. `pidAlive` (gate.go:240-258): add `defer p.Release()` (Windows handle leak).
f. Fix the inaccurate nolint comment at gate.go:392-393: O_EXCL closes the remove→open re-plant window (the preceding os.Remove handles pre-planted files) — say that.
g. Cross-user shared roots: gate files are created 0o600 (gate.go:322), so a second user hard-fails on a shared root like ~/.beads/shared-server/dolt. Document explicitly on `ForPhysicalRoot` that cross-user shared roots are unsupported with 0600 gate files and will fail with EACCES (do NOT widen to 0666 without an owner decision).
h. Document on `ForPhysicalRoot` the derived invariant that callers must not replace `.beads` itself while an in-`.beads` physical root (e.g. `.beads/embeddeddolt`) is gated — the gate file lives beside the guarded dir inside `.beads`.

### 3. Tests to add
- Sidecar with a known-dead PID: assert busyDetail reports it as stale in BOTH Shared and Exclusive modes (covers 2c; pidAlive currently at 54.5% coverage, busyDetail/readInfo untested).
- Case-variant dedupe: on a case-insensitive-capable setup this is hard to test portably; at minimum unit-test the comparison-key function directly for the windows/darwin lowering behavior.
- `ExclusiveHolder` error-return contract (currently only held/free branches tested): e.g. unreadable gate file → error, not "not held".

## Validation
- `gofmt -l` clean; `golangci-lint run ./internal/workspacegate/...` if available, else `go vet`.
- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -tags gms_pure_go -race ./internal/workspacegate/`
- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...` and GOOS=windows / GOOS=darwin cross-builds.
- Full `go test -tags gms_pure_go ./...` is NOT required here (verify queue will run it); run the package tests plus `go build`.

<result>Done. Commit `a9cfebc25` on `feat/psxg5-proxy-identity` in `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/fix-5013` (not pushed, as instructed).

## Changes per finding

**Blocking**
- **B1** `internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/endpoint.go` — `cleanupOrphanBackend` now kills, explicitly closes the handle, *then* calls `waitForRecordedProcessExit`, mirroring shutdown.go; the old `defer Close` kept the dead PID allocated on Windows so recovery always timed out.
- **B2** `internal/procid/procid_windows.go` — `tokenForProcess` checks `GetExitCodeProcess` != STILL_ACTIVE first and returns a new `errProcessExited` sentinel (covered by `IsProcessGone`); `Verify` maps it to `(false, nil)`. The invariant "Verify==true implies running" now holds everywhere: Capture/Open/Handle.verify all inherit the check.
- **B3** `internal/procid/procid_linux.go` — `Open` opens the pidfd *before* token verification; the pidfd pins the PID number so the post-open Verify is race-free. ENOSYS falls back to the old verify-first path (documented residual race).
- **B4** same file — `PidfdSendSignal` ESRCH on a fatal signal returns success, matching the fallback path; Windows `Signal` similarly treats exited-target as success.
- **B5** `shutdown.go` — `CanForceStopUnverified` now accepts refusals where each side is nil-or-unverifiable (proxy-only, backend-only, or paired). `force_stop.go` — `ForceStopUnverified` runs the identical inspect/signal/quarantine procedure on `proxy-child.pid` under `proxy-child.lock`; `ForceStopReport` gains a `Backend` sub-report and `cmd/bd/dolt.go` surfaces it in JSON (`backend` object) and human output.
- **B6a** new `unverified_process_{linux,windows,darwin}.go` — before signaling, the live PID's command line must contain rootDir (Linux `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, Darwin `ps -o args=`); Windows cannot read a foreign cmdline and refuses with an error naming the manual quarantine remedy (spec-sanctioned refuse-on-unknown).
- **B6b** — one stable handle (Linux pidfd — which pins the PID number; Windows `OpenProcess` handle) spans basename inspection, scope check, kill, and exit confirmation; `os.FindProcess` double-lookup removed.

**Should-fix**
- **S1** `control.go` — accept failures never close the listener or feed the errgroup; capped exponential backoff (10ms→5s) with logging, interruptible on Close; `Errors()` channel and the server.go watcher goroutine removed. Test renamed to `TestControl_AcceptLoopSurvivesPersistentErrors` pinning the new behavior.
- **S2** `force_stop.go` — `requireUnverifiableRecord` returns the `identity.RootID` error instead of failing open.
- **S3** `endpoint.go` — `killSpawnedChild` falls back to `cmd.Process.Kill()` (tolerating `os.ErrProcessDone`) when the verified handle is nil.
- **S4** `endpoint.go` — handshake check relaxed to `reply.Schema < pidfile.SchemaV2`.
- **S5** `procid_windows.go` — `errors.Is(err, windows.ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER)`.

**Tests added**: pidfd ESRCH-after-exit success + Open-after-reap gone-classification (`procid_linux_test.go`); paired-legacy Shutdown→CanForceStop→ForceStop end-to-end, foreign-workspace `bd` refused, updated helpers to live under the workspace root (`force_stop_linux_test.go`); schema-v3 handshake adoption (`endpoint_security_test.go`); Windows Verify-after-terminate-with-held-handle (`procid_windows_test.go`, compile-checked via GOOS=windows vet); CanForceStop table updated. One existing e2e helper (`proxied_local_identity_lifecycle_linux_test.go`) now references the workspace in its cmdline via its logpath, modeling a real pre-upgrade proxy's `--root` arg.

## Validation
- `gofmt -l` clean; `go vet` clean for linux, and GOOS=windows / darwin (compiles all test files).
- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/procid/... ./internal/storage/dbproxy/...` — **all ok**; also green under `-race` with CGO.
- Cross-compile `GOOS=windows` and `GOOS=darwin` `go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...` — OK.
- `./cmd/bd -run 'Proxied|ForceStop|Shutdown|DoltStop'` — ok. Gated lane `BEADS_TEST_PROXIED_LOCAL=1` (local dolt present) `^TestManagedLocalProxied` — **all 7 pass** (one subtest initially failed against the new B6a scoping; fixed by the e2e helper cmdline change above).
- Full `./cmd/bd` suite with CGO: 44 failures, all verified **pre-existing** — a representative subset fails identically at the base commit `d53a1ae19` in a clean detached checkout (host-environment leakage: global Claude-hook install output, host config.yaml, worktree-sensitive init/list/notion/tips tests), and the `TestMigrate*` cluster passes standalone on my tree.

**Not completed**: nothing from the spec. Out-of-scope items untouched except the mandated code comment on the birth-token capture-after-Start race (added in `forkExecChild`).

Resolve in favor of BOTH: keep 5013's non-fatal control accept loop and 5024's port-0 bind-and-hold handoff. After rebase, `go build` + the dbproxy package tests must pass before starting the findings below.

## Findings to fix (from two independent reviews of b7f86ddfd)

### F1 (MAJOR): managed listener policy must cover the whole YAML config, not just listener.host
`cmd/bd/proxied_server.go:440-466` (`validateManagedListenerHost`). Dolt honors `remotesapi.port` (all-interfaces HTTP+gRPC), `cluster.remotesapi.port` (same), and `listener.socket`, none of which are validated — a config with `listener.host: 127.0.0.1` plus `remotesapi: {port: 8080}` passes and exposes the root/empty-password DB to the network.
Fix: extend the check to reject, in managed mode: non-nil `RemotesapiConfig.Port_`, non-nil `ClusterConfig`, and non-empty `ListenerConfig.Socket`. Rename the function (e.g. `validateManagedServerConfigPolicy`) to reflect whole-config scope. Same remediation-text style as the host error.

### F2 (MAJOR, policy decision made by orchestrator): require an explicit numeric loopback host
Current code accepts an omitted host but rejects explicit `localhost` — an indefensible asymmetry, and the accepted omitted form is WORSE: `servercfg.CheckForUnixSocket` returns `/tmp/mysql.sock` whenever `Host() == "localhost"` (which is the default for omitted), silently opening a shared-namespace socket.
DECISION: managed-mode policy is an explicit numeric loopback IP, nothing else. Reject omitted host, reject `localhost` (keep that rejection), reject any hostname. Remediation text: `set listener.host to 127.0.0.1 (or another 127.0.0.0/8 / ::1 loopback address)`. This also kills the unreachable dead-code branch at :448-455 (`net.ParseIP("localhost")` is always nil). Managed configs are machine-generated with an explicit IP already, so the only breakage is hand-edited configs, which now get an actionable error. Keep accepting `::1`, `127.x.y.z`, `::ffff:127.0.0.1`; keep rejecting `0.0.0.0`, `::`.

### F3 (MAJOR + simplification): one interpolation-aware validation call instead of five
`ensureProxiedServerConfig` calls the validator at proxied_server.go:288, 331, 341, 363 and `renderProxiedServerConfig:539`. The :341 call sees raw `${VAR}` text, so a marker config with `host: "${BEADS_HOST}"` hard-fails even when it expands to 127.0.0.1 — contradicting the documented degrade-gracefully contract at :310-318.
Fix: rename the body to an unexported `ensureProxiedServerConfigLocked` (or similar), have the exported entry point run ONE `validateProxiedServerConfig(path)` (interpolation-aware via `YamlConfigFromFile`) on the resolved path before returning, and delete the scattered calls. Every path — generated, marker, hand-edited — then gets the same interpolation-aware policy check.

### F4 (MAJOR, from cross-vendor pass): startup interval not fenced by the stop epoch
`internal/storage/dbproxy/proxy/server.go:107-109` (line numbers pre-rebase). If `bd dolt stop` runs after the child acquires proxy.lock but before proxy.pid is written, the startup marker removed here was the only record identifying the in-progress start; a slow managed doltConfigure/doltInit can outlast both shutdown waits and then publish a running proxy AFTER the stop returned.
Fix: keep the in-progress marker (or an equivalent record) until the v2 identity is published, OR have the child re-check the stop epoch immediately before publishing proxy.pid and abort if it advanced. Either is acceptable; pick the one that fits the existing epoch mechanism with the least new state, and add a test if practical (a fake-slow backend hook exists in the test helpers — check proxied_local_helpers_test.go).

### F5 (minors, all in scope)
a. `endpoint.go:370-375` (pre-rebase numbers): non-zero-port child exit is misattributed to "could not listen on port %d". Check `exec.ExitError` for `proxy.LockHeldExitCode` (75) and keep lock-race wording for that case; otherwise include `opts.LogFilePath` in the message so the real listen error is findable.

c. `validateManagedProxiedServerConfigAtInit` (proxied_server.go:472-486) ignores `--proxied-server-root-path` because the flag isn't in the sidecar yet at validation time. Thread the flag value into the helper (or validate after the sidecar is persisted).

e. - Policy table test: remotesapi.port set → rejected; cluster present → rejected; listener.socket set → rejected; omitted host → rejected; `localhost` → rejected; `127.0.0.1`/`::1`/`127.42.0.9`/`::ffff:127.0.0.1` → accepted; `0.0.0.0`/`::` → rejected.

- F5c: `bd init --proxied-server --proxied-server-root-path <dir>` with a bad config in <dir> fails at init.

- `BEADS_TEST_PROXIED_LOCAL=1` gated lane if local dolt available (`command -v dolt`): `go test -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/bd -run '^TestManagedLocalProxied'` with CGO_ENABLED=1.

**Whole-config listener policy** — the managed-mode check validated only \`listener.host\`, but dolt also honors \`remotesapi.port\` and \`cluster.remotesapi.port\` (both bind all interfaces) and \`listener.socket\` — so a config with a loopback host plus \`remotesapi: {port: 8080}\` passed policy while exposing the root/no-password DB to the network. **Host policy made coherent** — the old code accepted an omitted host but rejected explicit \`localhost\`, and the accepted form was strictly worse: dolt's \`CheckForUnixSocket\` opens \`/tmp/mysql.sock\` whenever the effective host is \`localhost\` (the omitted-host default). # Proxied-Dolt campaign: three-PR review-and-fix sweep (2026-07-26)

**Session goal:** "anything we can do today to help push the proxied dolt initiative along?"

**Answer found:** the bottleneck was three campaign PRs sitting CI-green, mergeable,
and completely unreviewed. All three got a two-vendor adversarial review
(Claude Opus reviewer agents + `codex-agent reviewer --diff` on gpt-5.6-sol),
a same-day fix batch, and a pr-babysit handoff.

## Outcomes

| PR | Bead tail | Verdict | Fix head | Disposition |
|----|-----------|---------|----------|-------------|
| gastownhall/beads#5013 (psxg.5 proxy identity) | mybd-psxg.5 | NEEDS-FIXES → fixed | a9cfebc25 | pushed, handed off (squash) |
| gastownhall/beads#5024 (psxg.5 listener policy, **stacked on #5013**) | mybd-xf2k | NEEDS-FIXES → fixed | d83434010 (rebased onto a9cfebc25) | pushed --force-with-lease, handed off; merge AFTER #5013 |
| gastownhall/beads#5046 (psxg.2 workspace gate part 1) | mybd-hy3x | primitive land-ready; OpenGated blocked | 4ddaf4e28 | split to primitive-only, pushed, handed off |

Full-suite `make test` verification queued for all three heads (verify-babysit drains).

## Review highlights (cross-vendor found disjoint defects, again)

- **#5013 Claude:** Windows handle held across `waitForRecordedProcessExit` made
  crashed-proxy recovery fail unconditionally; Windows `Verify` counted dead
  processes as alive; root-ID mismatch had no CLI recovery; `--force` could
  SIGKILL an unrelated `bd`. **Codex:** pidfd opened after token verification
  (PID-reuse kill race); paired legacy records locked out of the forced recovery
  they exist for; `PidfdSendSignal` ESRCH misreported as failure.
- **#5024 Claude:** listener policy checked only `listener.host` while
  `remotesapi.port`/`cluster`/`listener.socket` bypassed it (all-interfaces or
  `/tmp/mysql.sock` exposure); omitted-host accepted while `localhost` rejected.
  **Codex:** startup interval not fenced by the stop epoch (stop could return,
  then the child publishes a running proxy). Policy decision: managed mode now
  requires an explicit numeric loopback IP.
- **#5046:** the gate primitive survived targeted attack (lock ordering, crash
  recovery, TOCTOU all sound); both blockers were in the bolted-on `OpenGated`
  API (wrong physical-root derivation vs the store's 4-layer mode resolution;
  gate skipped entirely with no metadata.json). Decision recorded on mybd-psxg.2:
  part 1 = primitive only; OpenGated returns in part 2 on a shared resolver.
  Carryover code preserved in session scratchpad `opengated-part2-carryover.md`.

## Follow-up beads filed

- mybd-7qp5 — control-handshake HMAC challenge-response + local-user DoS surface (P2)
- mybd-b56a — root-identity robustness (renamed roots, case variants) via os.SameFile (P2)
- mybd-nsg1 — Windows CI lane for proxied lifecycle tests (P2)
- mybd-fgqv — **triage rescued staged proxied work found in bd-main** (P1; see below)

## Rescue: crashed-session work found in bd-main

bd-main was detached at local-only a8784aebf (2026-07-23) with a staged,
never-committed 194-file changeset (+13588/−1040): proxied-server routing for
maintenance commands (gc/ping/compact/cleanup + integration tests), the
`proxied-local-smoke.yml` upstream workflow (psxg.1's un-PRed CI wiring), and a
CAS proposal doc. None of it is on origin/main. Preserved verbatim as branch
`rescue/staged-proxied-work-20260726` (93410c16b) via `commit-tree` — the
bd-main index/worktree were left untouched. Owner started a separate agent on
mybd-fgqv mid-session; this session made no further bd-main changes.

## What I noticed that isn't on any list

- The `.githooks` clobber pattern (tracked pre-push/prepare-commit-msg hooks
  overwritten, extra untracked hook files dropped) appeared in TWO places:
  bd-main root and the `psxg5-proxy-identity` worktree. Something — likely a
  `bd hooks install` variant or the Entire CLI — is rewriting tracked hooks in
  beads checkouts. Patches preserved in session scratchpad
  (`psxg5-worktree-githooks-dirty.patch`, `worktree-cruft/`). Worth a bead if it
  recurs.
- `mybd-uiiu`'s verify run failed today (exit=1, log in `.verify-logs/`) — that
  lane is another session's in-progress work; not chased here.
- pr-handoff attached #5013's tail to mybd-psxg.5 itself (external-ref set by a
  prior session). When the patrol merges #5013 it may close psxg.5 while #5024
  (same bead's scope) is still in flight — #5024's own tail mybd-xf2k plus the
  follow-up beads carry the remainder, but the campaign epic should not be
  considered psxg.5-complete until BOTH merge.

_claude-fable-5-medium on behalf of maphew_
